name: Sikaflex Fillet
paste:
SIKAFLEX® FILLET: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikaflex® Fillet, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sikaflex_fillet.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikaflex® Fillet where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikaflex® Fillet is a one-component, fast curing, flexible fillet joint sealant for use in professional waterproofing applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikaflex®-Fillet Joint is ideally suited to, and forms part of, Sika's waterproofing system. Sikaflex® Fillet is designed for use as a fillet joint for movement junctions (wall to wall, wall to floor) in waterproofing installations.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikaflex® Fillet
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Polyurethane fillet joint sealant
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - One-component, ready to use
    - Permanent flexible
    - Non Corrosive
    - Very good adhesion to many substrates
    - Excellent workability
    - High tear resistance
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane
    - Colour: Concrete Grey
    - Density: ~1.3 kg/l
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Movement capability: ±10%
    - Skinning time: ~40 minutes (+23°c & 50% relative humidity)
2.6 Joint design. The joint width must be designed to suit the movement capability of the sealant. In general the joint width must be greater than 10 mm and less than 35 mm. A width to depth ratio of 2 : 1 must be maintained for joints over 12mm wide with a minimum depth of 8mm. All joints must be properly designed and dimensioned by the specifier and the main contractor in accordance with the relevant standards. Backing: Depending on application closed cell, polyethylene foam backing rods or open cell foam backing rod must be used.
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 600ml Sausages (20 sausages per box)
    - Shelf life: 12 months from the date of production if the storage conditions are met.
    - Storage conditions: Must be stored in original, undamaged, sealed container in dry conditions protected from direct sunlight and at temperatures between +10°c and +25°c.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and homogeneous, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. Sikaflex® Fillet adheres without primers and/or activators. However, for optimum adhesion and critical, high performance applications, such as on multi-story buildings, highly stressed joints, extreme weather exposure or water immersion, the following priming and/or pretreatment procedures shall be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, galvanised steel, powder coated metals or glazed tiles have to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205, wiped on with a clean towel. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours). Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc, also have to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205,wiped on with a clean towel. After the necessary flash-off time, use a brush to apply Sika® Primer-3 N and allow a further flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours) before sealing the joints. PVC has to be cleaned and pre-treated using Sika® Primer-215 applied with a brush. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks shall be primed using Sika® Primer-3 N applied with a brush. Before sealing, allow a flash-off time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours). For more detailed advice and instructions please contact the local Sika Technical Services Department.
    - Note: Primers are adhesion promoters. They are neither a substitute for the correct cleaning of a surface, nor do they improve the strength of the surface significantly.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Curing rate: ~3-4mm per 24 hours (+23°c & 50% relative humidity)
4.3 Application method / tools.
    - Sikaflex® Fillet is supplied ready to use.
    - After the necessary substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth and apply any primer if necessary. Insert a foil pack into the sealant gun and extrude Sikaflex® Fillet into the joint making sure that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoids any air entrapment. Sikaflex® Fillet sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion. It is recommended to use masking tape where exact joint lines or neat lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time. Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surfaces. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.4 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Hardened / cured material can only be mechanically removed.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Elastic sealants may not be over painted with rigid or less flexible coatings.
    - Compatibility testing of proposed coatings must be undertaken to ensure suitability.
    - If there is no history of a particular coating/paint being applied over cured Sikaflex® Fillet for a period of six months or more, an overpaintability test should be made to determine:
    - That the paint dries properly within the expected time frame.
    - That if the paint film dries satisfactorily it is not subsequently softened and/or stained where it comes into contact with the Sikaflex® Fillet when exposed to the heat of the sun.
    - That the adhesion of the paint/coating is satisfactory.
    - Colour deviations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures, UV-radiation. However a change in colour will not adversely influence the technical performance or the durability of the product.
    - Do not use Sikaflex® Fillet as a glass sealer, on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on building materials which might bleed oils, plasticizers or solvents which could attack the sealant.
    - Sikaflex® Fillet should be used with care resealing joints that were previously filled with silicone sealant. Consult our Technical Department.
    - Do not use Sikaflex® Fillet to seal swimming pools.
    - Only use in well ventilated areas
    - Do not mix with or expose uncured Sikaflex® Fillet to substances that may react with isocyanates, especially alcohols which are often components within e.g. thinners, solvents, cleaning agents and formwork releasing compounds. Such contact could interfere or prevent the cross linking curing reaction of the material.
    - Epoxy resin coatings should be fully cured prior to the application of the adhesive / sealant as the uncured amine component could inhibit the cure of polyurethane adhesives / sealants.
4.6 Further information.
    - Safety Data Sheet (SDS)

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5°C to +35°C
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5°C to +35°C
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - Colour deviations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures, UV-radiation. However a change in colour will not adversely influence the technical performance or the durability of the product.
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikaflex® Fillet, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/sikaflex_fillet.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikaflex® Fillet, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/r/sds-sikaflex-fillet.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
